definitions.gloss: to scramble for; to fight over; to compete for
definitions.explanation: To struggle with others to take possession of something. Formed from {奪|うば}う (to seize) + {合|あ}う (reciprocal suffix), indicating mutual competition or a contest over something.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちがおもちゃを{奪|うば}い{合|あ}っている。
examples.english: The children are fighting over a toy.

examples.japanese: {限定|げんてい}{商品|しょうひん}を{客|きゃく}たちが{奪|うば}い{合|あ}った。
examples.english: Customers scrambled for the limited-edition items.

examples.japanese: {各社|かくしゃ}が{優秀|ゆうしゅう}な{人材|じんざい}を{奪|うば}い{合|あ}う{状況|じょうきょう}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: Companies continue to compete fiercely for talented workers.

notes:
FORMS:
Compound verb from {奪|うば}う (to seize, to snatch) + {合|あ}う (reciprocal suffix). The ～{合|あ}う pattern indicates that two or more parties are performing the action toward each other.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {席|せき}を{奪|うば}い{合|あ}う (to scramble for seats)
- ボールを{奪|うば}い{合|あ}う (to fight for the ball)
- {市場|しじょう}を{奪|うば}い{合|あ}う (to compete for market share)

USAGE:
Can describe both physical struggles (children fighting over a toy) and abstract competition (companies vying for talent). The word carries an intensity beyond simple {競|きそ}う (to compete).
